title: Opinions: creer que and no creer que

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *creo que* + indicative and *no creo que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 7. Historians disagree about why revolutions happen, so this lesson is full of opinions. Here you use the present tense: *Algunos historiadores creen que la desigualdad es la causa*; *otros no creen que la pobreza explique una revolución*.

items.spanish: Algunos historiadores creen que la desigualdad es la causa principal.
items.english: Some historians believe that inequality is the main cause.

items.spanish: Otros historiadores no creen que la pobreza explique una revolución.
items.english: Other historians do not believe that poverty explains a revolution.

items.spanish: No todos creen que esa explicación sea suficiente.
items.english: Not everyone believes that this explanation is enough.

items.spanish: Muchos creen que no hay una sola causa.
items.english: Many believe that there is not a single cause.

sections.content: *Creer que* is followed by the indicative (*es*, *explica*). *No creer que* is followed by the subjunctive (*sea*, *explique*). Watch the second case: *Muchos creen que no hay una sola causa* keeps the indicative, because the verb *creen* is affirmative.
